staffing_gap.caveat: Staff positions come from the same scaffold as the movement data. A camera sees people, not job titles -- separating staff from shoppers on real footage needs uniforms, a badge or a roster joined on shift times, and the accuracy of that step caps everything on this screen. No individual employee is identified.

gaze_heatmap.caveat: Real gaze annotations from retail_gaze (11 subjects, 42 sessions). Directional only: gaze was scripted rather than natural browsing, subjects wore face masks, and the product masks the dataset references were not shipped, so attention cannot be tied to a specific product.

carr_engagement_mix.caveat: Measured from CARR's own annotations (CC BY 4.0, doi:10.6084/m9.figshare.29470079.v3) -- no model inference. Frames are independent samples from a single tilted camera per store, so this is an engagement MIX, not a conversion funnel, and positions are normalised camera-frame coordinates, not floor metres. Class volumes reflect how the dataset was collected, not how often each behaviour happens in a real shop.

carr_motion.caveat: Produced by running pretrained YOLO11 + ByteTrack over CARR's own video clips -- the same detect-and-track path that would run on Madhar Sha's cameras. Speeds are a fraction of the frame per second, not metres per second: without camera calibration there is no scale, and clips are isolated shelf interactions rather than continuous store footage. Note also that the tracker follows every person in a clip while the label describes only the primary subject, so each class carries some background traffic -- the effect below is measured despite that contamination, not in its absence.

track_quality.caveat: Measured by running pretrained YOLO11 + ByteTrack over 18 CARR clips spread across 10 stores and all six behaviour classes -- the same detect-and-track path that would run on Madhar Sha's cameras. Read every figure as an optimistic ceiling: CARR clips are isolated 45-second snippets with usually one person in frame, so a track cannot outlive its clip and has little chance to be confused with a second shopper. Continuous store footage will be worse, not better.
